content:
An odd prime \(p\) is a sum of two primes only if one summand is \(2\), so \(p-2\) must be prime.  
It is a difference of two primes only if the subtracted prime is \(2\), so \(p+2\) must be prime.

Thus \(p-2,p,p+2\) must all be prime. Among three consecutive odd numbers spaced by \(2\), one is divisible by \(3\), so that one must be \(3\). The only valid case is:

\[
p-2=3,\quad p=5,\quad p+2=7.
\]

Check: \(5=2+3=7-2\).

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
